title: fix(android): release stale camera activity after destruction
body:
Fixes #195636

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android camera capture retains a destroyed Activity while the longer-lived runtime waits for a replacement Activity to attach.

## User Impact

Camera capture releases its stale Activity reference after destruction, while ordinary background/foreground transitions and a replacement Activity keep working. No configuration changes or user action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the attached lifecycle owner until destruction, remove the old observer when replacing it, and reject already-destroyed owners. Clear the reference only when the destroyed owner is still current. Existing foreground admission and active-capture cancellation remain unchanged.

This applies the exact parent-to-commit patch from [d38c7c12db5e61c273486053908709dcfe691b4c](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/d38c7c12db5e61c273486053908709dcfe691b4c) onto current main without implementation rewrites.

## Evidence

- Fresh isolated validation on published head `caf93bcd6830f0b455179d252c86be3120d350f4`: `CameraCaptureOwnershipTest` passed 7/7 Play and 7/7 third-party cases, with no skips. The repository Gradle tasks compiled production and test sources in a secretless, network-disabled rootless Podman runner using JDK 21, Node 24.22.1 and Gradle 9.7.1.
- Matched pre-fix control: only `CameraCaptureManager.kt` was restored from base `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`, retaining identical published regression-test bytes. Both new regressions failed for the intended lifecycle reasons; the five existing sibling tests passed. Restoring the fix returned Play to 7/7 passing before the third-party run. Raw XML, exits and source hashes were checked; the source was restored exactly. This is baseline production with the new regression fixture, not a claim that the base already contained those tests.
- Existing exact-head [CI run 42561181245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42561181245) passed, including both Android test variants, ktlint, 4KB/16KB native checks and the aggregate gate. Its two uploaded ownership-suite XML reports also contain 7 passes each. Those are reused hosted results, separate from the fresh local executions; CI executed historical synthetic merge `dcb0b468165e0b2fa0077f602a9a3e8ce84d32fa`, not today's composed main.
- Fresh full committed-range local ClawSweeper source review found no actionable code or security findings. The complete manager, Activity/runtime attachment path and ownership tests were inspected. Current-main composition is conflict-free and the reviewed owner/test/caller inputs are unchanged; no current-main composed runtime run is claimed.
- [Contributor device trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195669#issuecomment-6751717276) reports real idle `MainActivity` destruction on Pixel 10 Pro Fold / Android 17: base retains the destroyed owner, head clears it to null, and a replacement attaches. Both short log excerpts match the published SHA256 manifest. Device execution, instrumentation and APK/source binding remain contributor-reported, not independently replayed.

Limits: the fresh tests exercise JVM/Robolectric lifecycle ownership, not a physical camera, installed-app/Gateway flow or full APK build. Unrelated Mermaid UI asset generation was excluded; protocol/i18n generation and normal Kotlin/Java/test compilation ran. Permissions, foreground admission, shared capture exclusion and active-capture cancellation remain covered by the unchanged sibling contracts. This has no rendered UI change.

Contributor: @saariuslystoned (Bobby Bones). ☁️
